cur-fossil-olduvai.dateNote: On 17 July 1959 Mary Leakey found the skull of "Nutcracker Man" (Paranthropus boisei) in this Tanzanian gorge. Its layers hold about 2 million years of stone tools and bones; the skull is about 1.8 million years old.

q48773720.summary: In the Uganda–Tanzania War, Tanzanian forces beat back a Ugandan and Libyan counter-attack near Lukaya, opening the road to Kampala and the fall of Idi Amin.

q672146.summary: A trail of footprints left in volcanic ash about 3.6 million years ago, showing that early human relatives walked upright.
q672146.dateNote: Found in 1978; published in Nature in 1979 (Leakey and Hay).

q798283.summary: Two logs joined by a cut notch, about 476,000 years old. They may be the oldest known wooden structure built by human relatives.
q798283.dateNote: Published in Nature in 2023 (Barham et al.).
